contexts.description: Next.js app shell, page routes and the top-level blueprint workspace: header, dock, legend, overlays, project switching and theming. Mounts the engine and wires global styles. Uses the Next.js App Router and hooks into the engine store.
contexts.name: app-shell

contexts.description: Typed loaders for app-structure data and the standard lens catalog, health and presentation. Defines what a built-in lens is and how it is loaded and checked.
contexts.name: core-data-standard

contexts.description: Framework-neutral route handlers for products, lenses, scans, waves, releases, proposals, triage, streams, structure, screenshots and the live plan. Mounted by both the Next app and the node server.
contexts.name: core-route-handlers

contexts.description: Canvas engine that owns camera, state, store, theming and text measurement for the blueprint drawing. It exposes the lens contract and lens mixing so the renderers and UI can colour the plan by lens. Consumed by the render layer and React components.
contexts.name: engine-core

contexts.description: Drawing routines that paint the floor plan, glyphs, flags, scans, tracks, patterns and illustrations onto the canvas. Includes the static cache and the dynamic layer for live simulation overlays. Driven by Engine state and lens colouring.
contexts.name: engine-render

contexts.description: Detail sheet and page views for a selected feature: business summary, screens, lens panel, code tree and general tab. Presents lens-specific findings in plain words with motion helpers.
contexts.name: feature-sheet

contexts.description: Ledger page with triage and matrix variants, waves composer/bar and lens authoring (chat, draft card, panel). Loads ledger and wave data through hooks and lets users compose waves and edit lenses.
contexts.name: ledger-core

contexts.description: Framework-free domain model: product, aggregates, layout, lenses, live feed/health/tracks, morning briefing, search, time view and the scan and train simulators. Powers the blueprint views and the checks.
contexts.name: model-simulation

contexts.description: Standalone node:http server that mounts the core handlers, plus the TS loader hooks used to run it. It also holds a Kettle simulation driver and a mount check that verifies the handlers are wired up the same way as in the Next app.
contexts.name: node-server

contexts.description: Cross-cutting guards: check-all runner, camera, chrome sizes, core purity, route guards, server, overlays, search, sim answers/orders/blockers/precedent, tokens, timeview and structure validation.
contexts.name: platform-checks

contexts.description: Side rail and wide workbench with plan, orders, agents, review and steer panels, plus the live steer, queue and track record widgets. Lets users direct agent swarms and review their work.
contexts.name: rail-workbench

contexts.description: Server-only services behind the handlers: job runner, lens writing, product registry/store, readiness, release building, waves, plan projection and the Kettle simulator.
contexts.name: release-api-services

contexts.description: Kettle sample dataset (structure, events, findings, swarm) plus the generators, converters and fake agent used to produce and verify demo data and screenshots.
contexts.name: sample-data-generators

contexts.description: Scan pipeline logic: jobs, scope, readiness, derivation, comparison, merge, views, live plan, swarm orchestration, waves, lens drafting, local-only guard and release building. Pure code reused by the server handlers.
contexts.name: scan-engine

contexts.description: Scan launcher menu and the browser-side client for starting scans, managing projects and building scan views and temporary lenses. Talks to the scan and products APIs.
contexts.name: scan-menu-client

contexts.description: JSON schemas for app-structure, events, lens manifests, plan, scan-wire and structure-envelope, with a generator that emits TS types and Unreal USTRUCTs. Includes a parity check and a stand-in Unreal header set that compiles the generated headers without the engine.
contexts.name: schema-definitions

contexts.description: Timeline strip that scrubs and replays a project's history with keyboard control and run playback. Includes check scripts for keys, run, scrub and size behaviour.
contexts.name: timeline-scrubber

contexts.description: Before/after comparison panel for release items: change map (worker computed), commit diff, screenshots, performance tables and metric strips.
contexts.name: train-compare

contexts.description: Release-train decision UI: pack table, item rows, decision bar, notes and keyboard map for accepting or rejecting items. Shared controls and marks are in ui/.
contexts.name: train-decision

contexts.description: Release-train evidence rules: screenshots, pixel comparison, performance measurement, quality rules and the wire format.
contexts.name: train-evidence

contexts.description: Release flow UI: stepper, version box, packaging, notes preview, sample toggles, job log and release history, with state kept in releaseState.
contexts.name: train-release

contexts.description: Executable checks for the scan, live, release-train, lens-manifest, Kettle simulator and fixture behaviour. Run via npm check scripts.
contexts.name: train-scan-checks

contexts.description: Variant registry, shared types and the base and subtle legend variants (expression, marks, tooling for screenshots and grids). Lets the blueprint legend be rendered in alternate visual encodings.
contexts.name: variant-framework

contexts.description: The bold (colour channels, palette, decor) and shaped (glyph shapes, icons) legend variants with their panels, styles, notes and screenshot/perf scripts.
contexts.name: variants-bold-shaped

contexts.description: Python-driven fidelity contracts, role maps, screenshot and performance capture that verify the rendered UI against contracts.
contexts.name: visual-fidelity

contexts.description: Per-asset art manifests for the VR light table (city backdrop, lamp agent, frame, studio props, survey pin) and the scripts that generate and score them. Manifests record evidence and hand-off metadata, and the scripts write them from lookdev and Trellis runs.
contexts.name: vr-art-pipeline

contexts.description: Concept docs and look-development data for the VR light table: plan, tech stack, reference sheet, Wolf plan and prop/state/style/pick JSON. Leonardo-based scripts generate and check lookdev images and write prop manifests.
contexts.name: vr-lookdev-docs

contexts.description: Unreal-side BpLink module that connects the VR light table to the blueprint server, with the VR README, the WP3.1 work-package notes and a check script. It consumes the generated schema headers and the server's plan and scan wire formats.
contexts.name: vr-unreal-bridge

contexts.description: Next.js App Router API route files that mount the core handlers into the web app, now including the live plan route.
contexts.name: web-api-mounts
